dedupe_keys.name: diffwofost differentiable pytorch implementation of the wofost crop growth model

description: A Python package that re-implements the WOFOST crop growth models in PyTorch so that gradients flow through the simulation, which the GitHub README says is meant for optimisation and data assimilation. It is developed in the DeltaCrop project, a collaboration between Wageningen University & Research and the Netherlands eScience Center; the Zenodo authors are Ioannis Athanasiadis, Sarah Alidoost, Francesco Nattino, Simone Ciarella, Michiel Kallenberg, Ron van Bree and Allard de Wit. Version 0.5.0 of 29 May 2026 added hybrid modelling with a notebook example and a differentiable, vectorised water balance (WaterbalanceFD) that supports the water-limited WOFOST 7.2 configuration. The code is free to install from PyPI or download from Zenodo (a 0.75 MB ZIP) under the CC BY 4.0 licence stated on the Zenodo record, with online documentation. Coverage is any location with weather, soil and crop parameters, as for WOFOST. Caveats: a young research package whose modules are still being ported, and the crops and processes covered in version 0.5.0 are not listed on the pages read. For simulation it lets crop parameters be fitted to satellite or yield data by gradient descent and lets a crop model sit inside a machine learning pipeline, for example to estimate drought or heat losses to farm output. A related catalogue record is PCSE with WOFOST, LINTUL3 and LINGRA.
